To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rapid (3+1)-D transverse plus longitudinal collective expansion of a dense gluon plasma reduces the azimuthal asymmetries due to jet energy loss in non-central A + A collisions to a level that is below the observed level by a factor of 2–3.

the observed azimuthal asymmetry of high p T hadrons in non-central A + A collisions, v 1 ( p T >3 GeV/ c ), is due to the anisotropy in the jet quenching, which is in turn due to the transverse expansion of the plasma.

the observed azimuthal asymmetry v 2 (2 GeV/  c < p T <6 GeV/ c ), ∼0.15 at RHIC, may be reduced substantially to v 2 ∼0.05 by the rapid transverse expansion of the plasma, if the plasma is assumed to expand with an average transverse velocity v x ∼0.6 c. This

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed azimuthal asymmetry due to quenching is consistent with the assumption of rapid transverse collective plasma expansion, but it is not conclusive evidence for it.
the observed azimuthal asymmetry is consistent with the assumption of a (1+3)D collective expanding plasma.
the observed azimuthal asymmetries are consistent with the picture of jet energy loss in a (3+1)-dimensional expanding plasma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the observed azimuthal asymmetry of high p T particles at RHIC is not only consistent with the picture that jet energy loss is the dominant source of suppression, but it is also a strong evidence for the existence of rapid transverse collective plasma expansion.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a (3+1)-dimensional expanding medium is needed to explain the observed asymmetry.
the azimuthal asymmetries in high p T particle production in heavy-ion collisions can provide a unique probe of the transverse expansion of the plasma.
a large azimuthal asymmetry due to spatially anisotropy in the energy loss of jets can be reduced substantially by the transverse collective expansion in A+A collisions.
